parts.title: Sonar Sweep
parts.summary: Count how many consecutive sea-floor depth measurements strictly increase relative to the immediately preceding reading.
parts.algorithmSummary: Generalized stride-W algebraic cancellation (d[i] > d[i - W], W=1 for Part 1, pre-built W=3 for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day01/shared/ (1.18 ms across 2,000 depth readings -> 1,711 increases): immutable SonarReport with exact BigInt windowSum, bounded streaming sweep trace, bathymetry SVG profile visualizer, differentially verified against an independent O(N*W) explicit BigInt window-sum oracle across W = 1, 2, 3, 5.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Algebraic telescoping cancellation reduces sliding-window sum comparison (sum[i..i+W-1] > sum[i-1..i+W-2]) to a single stride comparison d[i+W-1] > d[i-1] with zero addition overflow and zero shared-module edits for Part 2.
Adding a bounds-checked SonarReport.depthAt(index) accessor eliminates unreachable fallback branches under TypeScript's noUncheckedIndexedAccess while preserving 100% V8 branch coverage.

parts.title: Sonar Sweep
parts.summary: Count how many consecutive three-measurement sliding-window depth sums strictly increase across the sonar report.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2021/day01/shared/ with stride W = 3 algebraic cancellation (d[i] > d[i - 3], 0.79 ms across 2,000 depth readings -> 1,743 increases): eliminates overlapping terms d[i-2] + d[i-1] and IEEE-754 3-sum rounding loss on MAX_SAFE_INTEGER readings, differentially verified against an independent BigInt 3-sum oracle across 30 seeded sequences and rendered with the shared gold cancelled-overlap bathymetry visualizer.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Pre-building generalized stride-W domain and overlay highlight logic in day01/shared/ let Part 2 land with zero shared edits and ~180 LOC total across domain, tests, visualizer wrapper, and manifest.
Comparing entering vs exiting endpoints directly (d[i] > d[i-3]) avoids 3-term IEEE-754 precision loss at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER where naive Number summation collapses adjacent distinct window sums.

parts.title: Dive!

BigInt fixed-point coordinate scaling and aspect-adjusted BigInt aim-slope clamping prevent Infinity/NaN SVG projection faults even for > 2^1024 custom inputs.

parts.title: Dive!

parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2021/day02/shared/ binding AIM_NAVIGATION_POLICY into navigateCourse, traceCourse, and DiveTrajectoryVisualizer (1.09 ms across 1,000 commands -> 2,089,174,012): exact BigInt cubic product, gold aim sightline overlay, differentially verified across 50 seeded courses (including > 2^65 odd-low-bit magnitudes) against both a divide-and-conquer associative affine-monoid oracle and a direct imperative BigInt oracle.

learnings: Pre-building AIM_NAVIGATION_POLICY and the conditional gold aim ray in day02/shared/ enabled Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
An associative divide-and-conquer affine monoid (dh, dd, da) provides an algebraically independent differential oracle for non-commutative aim kinematics.

parts.title: Binary Diagnostic
parts.summary: Compute the submarine's power consumption by multiplying the most-common-bit gamma rate and least-common-bit epsilon rate across all binary diagnostic columns.
parts.algorithmSummary: Arbitrary-width BigInt column bit-tally in 2021/day03/shared/ (1.40 ms across 1,000 12-bit readings -> 3,309,596): immutable DiagnosticReport with subset counting/filtering pre-built for Part 2, polymorphic BitCriterion strategies, PowerRates with dynamic getters, 100%-stacked SVG column chart with branchless 64-column sliding window, differentially verified across 50 seeded fixtures up to 80 bits against a BigInt shift-and-mask oracle.

learnings: Putting countBitsAtColumn(col, subset?) and filterRowsByBit(col, bit, subset) directly on DiagnosticReport prepares Part 2's O2/CO2 iterative bit filtering with zero edits to report.ts.
Branchless sliding-window clamping (Math.max(0, Math.min(maxStart, active - half))) handles both narrow and > 64-bit reports cleanly with 100% V8 branch coverage.

parts.title: Binary Diagnostic
parts.summary: Iteratively filter binary diagnostic readings left-to-right by most-common (oxygen) and least-common (CO2) bit criteria until one candidate remains, returning their product.
parts.algorithmSummary: Iterative index filtering reusing 2021/day03/shared/ with unanimous-column guard selectFilterBit (1.53 ms across 1,000 12-bit readings -> 2,981,085): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, zero-derived-state RatingSelection/LifeSupportRates/LaneStepSnapshot, dual-lane mirrored SVG narrowing funnel & lane detail visualizer, differentially verified across 50 seeded fixtures (up to 72 bits) against an independent binary-prefix-trie oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N * W) worst-case (O(N) expected), O(N) candidate working set
learnings: Guarding unanimous columns (ones === 0 -> '0', zeros === 0 -> '1') before delegating to LEAST_COMMON_CRITERION prevents CO2 filtering from emptying the candidate pool when distinct remaining rows share a bit.
Testing an explicit asymmetric witness where oxygen locks before CO2 (['110', '100', '000', '001']) covers both early-lock branches symmetrically.

parts.title: Giant Squid
parts.summary: Determine which 5x5 bingo board wins first as numbers are drawn and return the product of its unmarked cell sum and the winning drawn number.

Returning Object.freeze(new PolicyBingoSolver(policy)) from a top-level class eliminates nested function closures inside solver factories.

Computing accumulator bounds strictly from policy-included segments prevents a huge skipped diagonal in Part 1 from unnecessarily triggering sparse fallback.

parts.title: Hydrothermal Venture

parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2021/day05/shared/ binding OCTILINEAR_POLICY into createVentSolver and VentFieldVisualizer (4.17 ms across 500 segments -> 21,466): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, linear-stride Uint32Array rasterization handles all four 45-degree diagonal quadrants without row wrap, differentially verified across 40 seeded PRNG fields (including half-lattice near-misses, 4-quadrant stars, collinear opposite diagonals, oblique decoys, sparse fallback, and P2 >= P1 monotonicity) against an independent raw Map oracle.

learnings: Pre-building OCTILINEAR_POLICY and convex-bounds linear-stride stepping (stride = sy * width + sx) in day05/shared/ let Part 2 ship in 4 lines of domain code with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Testing half-lattice non-crossing diagonals ((0,0)->(1,1) vs (1,0)->(0,1) -> 0) and sparse fallback mode assertion guards against continuous-intersection and dense-only bugs.

parts.title: Lanternfish

learnings: Modeling lanternfish cohorts as a frozen 9-tuple CohortTuple eliminates noUncheckedIndexedAccess fallback branches and achieves 100% V8 branch coverage with zero allocations inside advance(days).
shared/core's bigintLog2 already computes top-53-bit floating-point log2, yielding smooth overflow-proof Log2 growth curves past 2^1100.

parts.title: Lanternfish

An independent 1D lineage recurrence f(d) = f(d-7) + f(d-9) with single-fish lookup f(days - t) cross-checks both 9-bucket rotation and matrix exponentiation cleanly even above 2^64.

parts.title: The Treachery of Whales
parts.summary: Find the integer horizontal alignment position minimizing total linear fuel consumption across a swarm of crab submarines.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact BigInt discrete convex binary search using shared/core floorDiv and polymorphic FuelCostModel (LINEAR_FUEL_MODEL for Part 1, pre-built TRIANGULAR_FUEL_MODEL for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day07/shared/ (2.17 ms across 1,000 crabs -> 328,187): non-empty tuple CrabFleet, exact global-minimum anchor in buildFuelLandscape, contiguous ceilDiv swarm histogram & convex fuel-curve dual-panel SVG visualizer, differentially verified across 40 seeded PRNG fleets against both full-range brute-force and analytic median/mean oracles for both fuel models.
parts.complexity: O(N log R) time, O(N) space
learnings: Using shared/core floorDiv(lo + hi, 2n) prevents negative BigInt truncation loops on adjacent ranges like [-1n, 0n] while deterministically finding the leftmost global minimizer on even-median plateaus.

Explicitly inserting optimal.target into sampled fuel-landscape points guarantees landscape.minFuel === optimal.fuel so chart scaling never throws RangeError when uniform samples straddle the minimum.

parts.title: The Treachery of Whales

learnings: Pre-building TRIANGULAR_FUEL_MODEL and exact BigInt discrete convex binary search in day07/shared/ let Part 2 ship in 3 lines of domain code with zero shared edits.

For strictly convex triangular fuel, all minimizers lie inside {floorDiv(sum, n), floorDiv(sum, n) + 1n} (verified algebraically for negative sums too), providing an O(N) closed-form differential oracle.

parts.title: Seven Segment Search
parts.summary: Count how many times digits 1, 4, 7, or 8 (having unique active segment counts 2, 4, 3, or 7) appear in the four-digit seven-segment output values.
parts.algorithmSummary: Closed-form wire-frequency classification (e:4, b:6, f:9, c/a:8 split by mask1, d/g:7 split by mask4) with bijection validation and 10-pattern canonical round-trip verification in 2021/day08/shared/ (UNIQUE_DIGITS_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built DECODED_OUTPUT_SUM_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2; 4.00 ms across 200 displays -> 504): zero-derived-state SignalPattern/DisplayEntry/DecodedDisplay/DisplayTraceFrame, beveled 4-digit LED SVG & wire-frequency deduction visualizer, differentially verified across 40 seeded PRNG displays against an independent 7! = 5,040 Heap's-algorithm permutation oracle plus a frequency-sum-preserving forged wiring rejection test.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Direct frequency-sum fingerprinting is unsound on forged wirings (swapping a<->c in digits 1 and 5 preserves all 7 wire frequencies and all 10 canonical frequency sums yet admits zero bijections), whereas closed-form wire deduction + WireMapping bijection + 10-pattern round-trip verification is provably 100% equivalent to 7! search.

Because DisplayEntry enforces 10 distinct signal masks and WireMapping enforces a 7-bit bijection, verifying all 10 remapped signal masks are canonical digits is mathematically sufficient for bijectivity onto 0..9 without an unreachable duplicate-digit V8 branch.

parts.title: Seven Segment Search

learnings: Pre-building DECODED_OUTPUT_SUM_POLICY, WireMapping, and SevenSegmentVisualizer in day08/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 3 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Testing a stealth forged wiring that preserves all 7 wire frequencies plus canonical digits 1 and 4 verifies the 10-pattern canonical round-trip check deterministically.

parts.title: Smoke Basin
parts.summary: Find every low point in a 2D cavern heightmap that is strictly lower than all four orthogonal neighbors and return the sum of their risk levels (height + 1).
parts.algorithmSummary: Row-major 4-neighbor low-point scan and component-at-a-time iterative flat-Int32Array-queue BFS over height < 9 cells in 2021/day09/shared/ (LOW_POINT_RISK_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built LARGEST_BASINS_PRODUCT_POLICY with O(R*C) wave-depth counting sort for zero-churn Part 2; 6.65 ms across 100x100 grid -> 560): discriminated union LowPointScanFrame | BasinFloodFrame, HiDPI light-mode BathymetryCanvas resolving CSS tokens via getComputedStyle, differentially verified across 40 seeded PRNG heightmaps against three independent oracles (brute-force 4-neighbor scan, shared/core DisjointSet percolation, and Set<string> DFS).

Using a discriminated union LowPointScanFrame | BasinFloodFrame eliminates nullable-bag fields and keeps Part 1 and Part 2 traces cleanly typed with zero stored derived state.

parts.title: Smoke Basin
parts.summary: Find all 4-connected heightmap basins bounded by height-9 ridges and return the product of the sizes of the three largest basins.

learnings: Pre-building LARGEST_BASINS_PRODUCT_POLICY and BathymetryCanvas flood overlays in day09/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 3 lines with zero shared-module edits.

When using DisjointSet as a differential oracle on grids with walls, sizes must be collected strictly from roots of non-ridge cells because DisjointSet initializes every ridge cell as its own size-1 component.

parts.title: Syntax Scoring

learnings: Running upfront full-line validateBracketText before stack scanning rejects trailing invalid characters on already-corrupted lines (like '(]X') while making the stack loop a clean 2-branch open/close scan.
Storing only openStackIndices as the single source of truth cleanly derives matched/unclosed/clash character roles, expected closers, and base-5 BigInt autocomplete trails with zero state drift.

parts.title: Syntax Scoring

learnings: Pre-building AUTOCOMPLETE_MEDIAN_POLICY, AutocompleteScanFrame, and AutocompleteOutcome in day10/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Comparing 5^30 - 4 vs 5^30 - 1 in median sorting proves exact BigInt ordering even where IEEE-754 Numbers collide.

Using the 1x2 '05' grid (which enters an exact period-9 cycle and never synchronizes) deterministically tests FIRST_SYNC_STEP_POLICY's maxSyncSteps RangeError bound.

parts.title: Dumbo Octopus

Pairing a state-set cycle-detecting oracle with a 500-step bounded solver on proven non-syncing PRNG grids avoids spinning 100,000 steps per cycle and keeps the full differential test suite under 75 ms.

parts.title: Passage Pathing
parts.summary: Count all distinct paths from start to end through an undirected cave network where uppercase big caves may be visited any number of times and lowercase small caves at most once.
parts.algorithmSummary: Big-cave contraction into a weighted small-cave multigraph (explicitly preserving degree-1 big-cave self-loops w(s,s) while excluding transitions into start or out of end) paired with exact BigInt-bitmask memoized DP and polymorphic CaveVisitPolicy (NO_REVISIT_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built SINGLE_SMALL_REVISIT_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day12/shared/ (0.77 ms across 25 edges / 13 caves -> 3,369): bounded raw-graph DFS trace with derived findRevisitedSmallCave, BFS-layered quadratic-Bezier CaveGraphSvg visualizer, differentially verified across all 3 official examples and 35 seeded PRNG graphs for both Part 1 and Part 2 against an independent string-backtracking DFS oracle.
learnings: Contracting big caves into weighted transitions over non-big caves—including ordered self-pairs (u === v) for degree-1 big caves like LN-dc—cuts state space dramatically while staying 100% isomorphic for Part 2 single-small-cave revisits.
Guarding visitedSmall.delete(next) with if (!alreadyVisited) during raw-graph DFS trace backtracking prevents Part 2 revisits from erasing the earlier visit while still inside that cave.

parts.title: Passage Pathing
parts.summary: Count all distinct paths from start to end where at most one regular small cave may be visited twice, all other small caves at most once, start/end exactly once, and big caves arbitrarily often.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2021/day12/shared/ binding SINGLE_SMALL_REVISIT_POLICY into CavePathSolver and CaveVisualizer (0.96 ms across 25 edges / 13 caves -> 85,883): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, contracted small-cave multigraph (preserving degree-1 big-cave self-loops) + BigInt bitmask DP memoizing (u, budget, visitedMask), gold Revisited halo and badge in CaveGraphSvg, differentially verified across all 3 official examples (36, 103, 3509), self-loop topologies, and 30 seeded PRNG graphs against an independent raw-string backtracking DFS oracle.

learnings: Pre-building SINGLE_SMALL_REVISIT_POLICY, contracted self-loop weights w(s,s), and gold Revisited overlays in day12/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and counted 85,883 paths in under 1 ms.
Bounding seeded differential graphs to 3-4 small caves and 1-2 big caves prevents worst-case raw-DFS path explosions while still thoroughly verifying multi-big-cave loops and triangles in 13 ms.

parts.title: Transparent Origami
parts.summary: Fold a transparent coordinate sheet along its first horizontal or vertical crease and count the distinct visible dots after overlapping reflections merge.
parts.algorithmSummary: Canonical sorted-deduplicated DotSheet with O(log N) binary-search hasDot, overflow-safe injective reflection fold.value - (coord - fold.value), axis-polymorphic AXIS_ADAPTERS, and OrigamiPolicy (FIRST_FOLD_COUNT_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built 5x6 bitmap OCR ALL_FOLDS_CODE_POLICY with minX-1 fallback for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day13/shared/ (1.73 ms across 974 dots -> 818): discriminated OrigamiTraceFrame with zero stored derived state, adaptive scatter/pixel-tile HiDPI OrigamiSheetCanvas visualizer, differentially verified across 10 seeded sheets and a personal-scale 900-dot 12-fold 8-letter code against independent 2D boolean[][] and Set<string> oracles.
parts.complexity: O(N log N + N * F) time, O(N) space
learnings: Because reflection c -> k - (c - k) is strictly injective on c > k, two reflected dots can never collide with each other—an overlap occurs iff the reflected coordinate already exists in the stationary sheet.
Using fold.value - (coord - fold.value) instead of 2 * fold.value - coord keeps reflection overflow-free across the entire JS safe-integer range.

parts.title: Transparent Origami
parts.summary: Execute all horizontal and vertical origami folds on the transparent coordinate sheet and decode the resulting eight-capital-letter 5x6 bitmap activation code.

Scaling Log2 charts via bigintLog2(value + 1n) / bigintLog2(maxValue + 1n) prevents division-by-zero NaN on single-element templates (maxCount = 1n) and zero-spread traces while preserving 100% V8 branch coverage.

parts.title: Chiton
parts.summary: Find the lowest-total-risk 4-directional path from the top-left to bottom-right corner of a cavern risk grid (excluding start risk, including destination risk).
parts.algorithmSummary: Dial's 10-bucket circular-queue O(R*C) Dijkstra exploiting integer weights in 1..9 and the vertex-weight zero-stale-entries theorem (dist[next] === UNVISITED) with CavernPolicy tiling (PART1_POLICY tileFactor=1, pre-built PART2_POLICY tileFactor=5 for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day15/shared/ (2.44 ms across 100x100 cavern -> 755): O(V + maxDistance) prefix-sum wavefront & golden path-reveal trace, HiDPI ImageData CavernCanvas resolving CSS tokens via getComputedStyle, differentially verified across official 1x1 (40) & 5x5 (315) examples, UP/LEFT detour mazes, and 25 seeded PRNG grids against an independent shared/core MinHeap Dijkstra oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Because every edge (u, v) in Chiton has weight risk(v) depending solely on target v and Dial's pops vertices in non-decreasing distance order, each cell is discovered at most once—eliminating any unreachable stale-entry continue branch under 100% V8 coverage.
Precomputing settledCount and frontierCount via an O(V + maxDistance) distance-histogram prefix sum avoids O(frames * V) per-frame scans on 500x500 Part 2 caverns.

parts.title: Chiton

Because 5x5 tiling wraps 9 -> 1 in adjacent tiles, verifying non-monotonic UP/LEFT optimal moves on expanded maps requires double-9 barrier bands so the detour remains globally optimal across tile boundaries.

parts.title: Packet Decoder
parts.summary: Decode a hexadecimal BITS transmission into its nested literal and operator packet hierarchy and return the sum of all packet version numbers.
parts.algorithmSummary: Nibble-backed HexBitstream (private Uint8Array nibbles + BitCursor) and recursive-descent immutable AST (LiteralPacket with exact BigInt, OperatorPacket with lengthTypeId 0/1 and BitSpan) paired with polymorphic PacketPolicy and total OPERATOR_SPECS lookup table (VERSION_SUM_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built EVALUATE_EXPRESSION_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day16/shared/ (1.06 ms across 1,354 hex chars / 5,416 bits -> 977): O(1) pre-order/post-order DFS trace queries with zero per-frame Sets, hard-capped 64-bit BitSpanStrip + 120-row windowed PacketAstTree visualizer, differentially verified across all 7 Part 1 & 8 Part 2 official examples plus 30 seeded random AST round-trips against an independent binary-string oracle.
parts.complexity: O(B) time, O(H + P) space for B = 4H bits and P packets
learnings: Encoding DFS pre-order and post-order ranks directly on IndexedPacketNode makes per-frame decoded/reduced membership O(1) arithmetic (nodeId < decodedCount and postOrderRank < reducedCount) with zero per-frame Set allocations.
Hard-capping BitSpanStrip at 64 rendered bit cells and windowing PacketAstTree at 120 visible rows keeps DOM node count O(1) even on multi-kilobit transmissions and huge BigInt literals.

parts.title: Packet Decoder

learnings: Pre-building EVALUATE_EXPRESSION_POLICY, total OPERATOR_SPECS, and post-order reduction playback in day16/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and evaluated the 5,416-bit expression tree in 1.19 ms with zero shared edits.
Encoding 0n literals with a do-while nibble loop in synthetic round-trip fuzz generators guarantees 0n emits a single 5-bit terminal group (00000) rather than an empty payload.

parts.title: Trick Shot
parts.summary: Find the highest vertical y apex reached by any integer-velocity ballistic trajectory launched from (0, 0) that lands inside the target trench on at least one discrete step.
parts.algorithmSummary: Time-indexed exact axis decoupling with Int32Array interval prefix sums (xLoPrefix[yHi] - xHiPrefix[yLo - 1]) and polymorphic TrickShotPolicy (MAX_APEX_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built VALID_VELOCITY_COUNT_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day17/shared/ (0.54 ms -> 3,655): handles narrow non-stalling targets and stalling-vs-overshoot boundaries exactly without naive triangular-apex assumptions, lookahead loop guards for zero unreachable V8 branches, dual light-mode BallisticArcSvg + VelocityPhaseSpaceSvg playback visualizer, differentially verified against a brute-force 2D ballistic simulator across official examples (45 / 112), narrow non-stalling targets (1 / 12 and 0 / 1), and 15+ seeded PRNG target boxes.
parts.complexity: O(X log X + |Y| log |Y|) time, O(X + |Y|) space
learnings: Using lookahead bounds in computeXStepInterval (x + curVx <= xMax) prevents misclassifying a velocity that overshoots xMax on the exact step curVx reaches 0 as stalling inside the target.

Counting matching vx intervals per vy via Int32Array prefix sums (xLoPrefix[yHi] - xHiPrefix[yLo - 1]) solves both exact Part 1 apex (including narrow non-stalling trenches) and duplicate-free Part 2 counts in O(1) per vy.

parts.title: Trick Shot
parts.summary: Count every distinct integer initial launch velocity (vx, vy) from (0, 0) whose ballistic trajectory lands inside the target trench on at least one discrete step.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2021/day17/shared/ binding VALID_VELOCITY_COUNT_POLICY into TrickShotSolver and TrickShotVisualizer (0.54 ms -> 1,447 distinct velocities): zero edits to shared/ or part1/, O(1) per-vy interval overlap counts via Int32Array prefix sums (xLoPrefix[yHi] - xHiPrefix[yLo - 1]) avoiding multi-step hit double-counting, synchronized BallisticArcSvg + VelocityPhaseSpaceSvg phase-space sweep visualizer, differentially verified across the official example (112), 6 stalling/overshoot/gap/overlap boundary boxes, and 28 seeded PRNG target boxes against an independent 2D brute-force ballistic simulator.

learnings: Pre-building VALID_VELOCITY_COUNT_POLICY, Int32Array interval prefix sums, and VelocityPhaseSpaceSvg in day17/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and counted 1,447 velocities in 0.54 ms with zero shared edits.

Summing xLoPrefix[yHi] - xHiPrefix[yLo - 1] over disjoint vy intervals counts each hitting (vx, vy) pair exactly once by construction even when trajectories spend multiple consecutive steps inside the trench.

parts.title: Snailfish
parts.summary: Left-fold snailfish pair additions with explode-before-split reduction across all homework lines and return the final sum's recursive 3*left + 2*right magnitude.

Delegating trace operand selection to SnailfishPolicy.planTrace(homework) lets Part 1 and Part 2 share one unified trace loop with zero mode switches and without running Part 2's O(N^2) pair scan during Part 1.

Initializing bestMag = -1 and distinguishing pairs strictly by index (i !== j) rather than value equality handles all-zero and duplicate-line homeworks cleanly.

parts.title: Beacon Scanner
parts.summary: Reconstruct a contiguous 3D ocean trench map from 40 unoriented beacon scanner reports sharing >= 12 overlapping beacons under 24 proper cube rotations and count all unique beacons.
parts.algorithmSummary: Sorted Float64Array pairwise squared-distance fingerprint pre-filter (>= C(12,2) = 66 matches) + all-offsets 1D signed-axis voting across programmatic right-handed SO(3, Z) ROTATIONS_24 (det = +1) with exact 3D Set verification and polymorphic BeaconScannerPolicy (BEACON_COUNT_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built MAX_SCANNER_MANHATTAN_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day19/shared/ (32.22 ms across 40 scanners / 1,030 readings -> 465 unique beacons): zero-derived-state ScannerReport & TrenchMap, fixed-bounds 3D orthographic TrenchProjectionSvg + BeaconScannerVisualizer playback, verified on the exact official 5-scanner example (79 beacons / 3,621 max Manhattan), 24-rotation group axioms, decoy 1D tie-breaking, and det = -1 mirror-reflection rejection.
parts.complexity: O(N * M^2 log M + N^2 * M^2) time, O(N * M^2) space
learnings: Returning ALL qualifying 1D offsets (>= minOverlap) rather than only the argmax prevents duplicate single-axis coordinates from shadowing the true 3D translation offset.

Programmatically generating the 24 proper rotations via cross-product zSign = xSign * ySign * ((xAxis + 1) % 3 === yAxis ? 1 : -1) guarantees det = +1 and rejects det = -1 reflections that pass pairwise distance pre-filters.

parts.title: Trench Map
parts.summary: Apply 2 simultaneous 3x3 cellular-automaton image-enhancement passes over an infinite 2D plane (tracking infinite-void parity flips) and count all lit pixels.
parts.algorithmSummary: Pre-allocated double-buffered Uint8Array convolution with unconditional 2-cell halo stamping and rolling 3-bit horizontal row windows (w0/w1/w2 pre-loaded on newLeft-1..newLeft) paired with polymorphic EnhancementPolicy (PART1_POLICY = 2 steps, pre-built PART2_POLICY = 50 steps for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day20/shared/ (1.77 ms across 100x100 blinking-void personal input -> 5,400 lit pixels): explicit infinite-background parity tracking across all four (algo[0], algo[511]) regimes, RangeError guard on infinite-lit totalLitPixels, HiDPI ImageData TrenchMapVisualizer displaying the flashing Infinite Void halo, differentially verified against an independent sparse Set<string> + outsideBit oracle across 30 seeded grids and composition invariants.
parts.complexity: O(S * (H0 + 2S) * (W0 + 2S)) time, O((H0 + 2S) * (W0 + 2S)) space
learnings: Stamping a 2-cell background halo unconditionally before every enhancement step eliminates inner-loop bounds checks while preserving exact composition when an input image already starts with background === 1.
Pre-loading the 3-bit rolling row windows from columns (newLeft - 1, newLeft) before shifting in c + 1 avoids off-by-one shifts while cutting per-pixel reads from 9 to 3.

learnings: Pre-building PART2_POLICY (steps = 50), DEFAULT_MAX_TRACE_STEPS = 51, and double-buffered rolling 3-bit convolution in day20/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 4 lines and ran 50 passes over 40,000 cells in 6.13 ms with zero shared edits.

Using a naive 2D PixelBit[][] differential oracle instead of string-keyed Sets keeps 50-pass blinking-void verification under 10 ms while remaining completely independent of flat Uint8Array halo indexing.

parts.title: Dirac Dice
parts.summary: Simulate a two-player 10-space circular-track game with a deterministic 100-sided die (3 rolls per turn) until a player reaches score 1,000, returning losingScore * totalDieRolls.
parts.algorithmSummary: Direct turn-by-turn deterministic simulator with exact wrapped 100-sided die triplets paired with pre-built sparse-active forward wavefront exact BigInt DP (O(|active|) double-buffered reset + post-round per-space universe weights for zero-churn Part 2) in 2021/day21/shared/ (0.75 ms -> 929,625): zero stored derived state on DeterministicTurnFrame & QuantumTraceFrame, circular 10-space DiracTrackSvg reusing shared/core bigintLog2 for dual deterministic/quantum overlays, differentially verified across all 100 (1..10)^2 starting pairs against an independent O(1) period-10 algebraic cycle oracle for Part 1 and against an independent player-symmetry memoized BigInt DP oracle + round-by-round 27x conservation invariant for Part 2.
parts.complexity: O(T) Part 1 / O(P * S_active * 7) Part 2 time, O(1) Part 1 / O(100 * T^2) Part 2 space
learnings: Using plain bigint[] double buffers with O(|active|) zeroing on pop eliminates both BigInt64Array 2^64 overflow and TypedArray freeze hazards while emitting exact turn-by-turn multiverse wavefront and ring-density frames in one pass.
Reusing shared/core bigintLog2(weight + 1n) for quantum track glow scaling maps 0n -> 0 and 1n -> 1 monotonically without throwing or branching.
